title: Oncall handoff - Lucas Wright - 2026-03-04 (draft)
content:
TL;DR:
- Quiet night overall. One alert group flared (model-serving OOM) at 02:10 UTC; mitigated by scaling a dedicated pool and rolling a small config tweak (see incident notes below).
- Left a couple of temporary procedures to keep services stable while infra team rolls a kernel/driver patch next week.
- TODOs for next shift: check the rolling deploy status for dedicated pool resize (INFRA-589), verify nightly cost report for burst capacity.

Shift summary (lucid bullets, quick scan):
- 00:45 UTC: Routine lag spike on hosted-api route /v1/generate for model redwood-3b-quant. p95 spiked to ~1.1s (baseline ~0.35s). Auto-scaling kicked in, but a subset of pods experienced OOMs.
- 02:10 UTC: Alert group: model-serving OOM (alert: model-serving.memory.oom rate > 0.5/min). Affected: dedicated-pool-east-1 (4/12 nodes). Error pattern: KV cache grew unexpectedly for a small subset of requests (long-context conversations).
- 02:18 UTC: Quick mitigation: scaled dedicated-pool-east-1 from 12->18 nodes, enabled temporary kill-on-oom throttle on problematic pods, and rolled a config to enable KV cache capped size (cap=2GB) for redwood-3b-quant. Error rate dropped by 90% in 8m.
- 03:00 UTC: Follow-up: created INFRA-589 to track kernel/driver bump (suspected GPU driver memory accounting bug). Assigned to Priya (infra).

Current system status (what I care about next shift):
- dedicated-pool-east-1: nodes 18/18 healthy now, but new nodes not fully warmed (warm cache miss). Watch p50/p95 for the next 2 hours.
- hosted-api error-rate: 0.03% (acceptable) but watch for regrowth after traffic increase at 08:00 PST.
- Cost/billing: burst auto-cap used ~+12% last night — finance flagged for review. Link to sheet in INFRA-589.

Temporary procedures (write-up to follow into Confluence if we make permanent):
1) Temporary KV cache cap (safe fallback)
   - When model-serving OOM alerts trigger for redwood-3b-quant, set KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=2147483648 on the affected node group's config map.
   - Command (kubectl namespace=runtime):
     kubectl set env deployment/model-serving -n runtime KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=2147483648 --record
   - Rollout: deploy to 10% of pods first, monitor OOMs for 10m, then ramp to 100%.
   - Note: this reduces context caching and may increase token compute for long chat sessions. Inform product if latency regresses >15%.

2) Quick scale procedure for dedicated pool (emergency):
   - If >30% nodes show OOM within 10m, increase node count by +50% temporarily: aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name dedicated-pool-east-1 --desired-capacity <new_count>
   - After scaling, mark incident in JIRA as "mitigation in place" and create a follow-up task to revert to baseline once patch/monitoring confirms stability.

Runbook pointers (quick links):
- Model-serving incident playbook: Confluence: /display/SRE/Model+Serving+Playbook
- Dedicated pool scaling runbook: Confluence: /display/SRE/Dedicated+Pool+Ops
- Driver/kernel upgrade checklist: Confluence: /display/Infra/Driver+Upgrade

Escalation contacts (quick):
- Infra lead: Priya Menon (pager: +1-415-555-0123, slack @priya)
- Serving runtime: Mateo Ruiz (slack @mateo, GitHub: /mateo-ruiz)
- On-call support (secondary): Aisha Rahman (slack @aisha)

Commands & quick checks (copy-paste):
- Check pods OOMs last 1h: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=OOMKilled --namespace runtime --since=1h
- Pod memory usage (top): kubectl top pods -n runtime | sort -k3 -h | tail -n 30
- Check autoscaler activity: aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name dedicated-pool-east-1 --query 'Activities[0:5]'

Open questions / notes to self: (these are messy)
- Is INFRA-589 the right tracking ticket for the driver bump or do we split into a dedicated kernel-accounting bug ticket? (asked Priya)
- Need to confirm whether cap=2GB is safe for all models — might break a small internal eval. Ask research team before making permanent.
- Follow-up with finance about burst cost; might need to tune autoscaler cooldowns.

Post-shift TODO (for next oncall):
- Verify INFRA-589 progress and patch ETA (priority: high).
- Run the CT (smoke) for dedicated-pool after patch: run smoke-test-suite --tag dedicated-pool --region east-1
- Confirm rollback plan for KV cache cap if user-facing regressions observed.
- Check nightly cost report and tag any abnormal spots to /costs review sheet.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Sent quick ping to #sre-oncall at 02:25 with mitigation summary. Save that message link if needed for postmortem.
- Might add an alert to detect sudden growth in KV cache size per-request (metric idea: kv_cache_per_request_bytes p95 > 1.2MB).

If anything is urgent, slack @aisha or page Priya. Otherwise, normal handoff.

-- lucas
(Draft handoff; will tidy into Confluence if we need a persistent procedure)
